title: Anambra SASA Killing: Youths Storm Government House as Outrage Over Chinyeaka Ike's Death Grows
excerpt: Anambra youths marched to the state government house demanding justice after SASA operatives allegedly killed 26-year-old Chinyeaka Ike in Mgbakwu. Here is the full story.
content:
On Thursday evening in Mgbakwu, a quiet community in Awka North Local Government Area, a 26-year-old man was killed. His name was Chinyeaka Ike. He was the only son of his parents. He had recently married. His wife is expecting their first child next month.

![Anambra SASA Killing: Youths Storm Government House as Outrage Over Chinyeaka Ike's Death Grows](https://res.cloudinary.com/dhmtrmwva/image/upload/v1777933213/century-blog/blog/images/anambra-sasa-killing-youths-storm-government-house-as-outrage-over-chinyeaka-ike-s-death-grows-5a81e424-c983-4128-aad1-450f4fc03174.png)

By Friday morning, hundreds of youths were marching toward the Anambra State Government House in Awka, bearing his body alongside placards and green leaves, demanding the one thing his family cannot get back: justice.

What happened in Mgbakwu on the night of 1 May 2026 is still disputed in its exact details. What is not disputed is that a young man is dead, that operatives of a state-backed security unit are accused of killing him, and that an entire community has reached a breaking point.

---

## What Happened: The Incident in Mgbakwu

The incident reportedly occurred around 8 PM to 10 PM on Thursday evening when operatives of the Anambra State Special Anti-Touting Squad, widely known as SASA, and a local security group called Udogachi, conducted a raid in the Mgbakwu community.

Accounts of exactly how Chinyeaka Ike died vary. Some witnesses reported he was stabbed. Others said he was shot. A source from within the SASA team told The News Chronicle that the operatives came under attack from youths in the community during the raid, which was described as part of ongoing efforts to rid the area of hard drugs, and that the deceased was injured in the response.

Community members gave a different account. Multiple witnesses said Ike was not involved in any confrontation. One version of events described him as standing by the roadside with his wife when a bullet discharged from the gun of a nearby operative struck him. Another described a more direct confrontation between operatives and residents.

What is consistent across every account is the outcome: Chinyeaka Ike, described by those who knew him as the only son of his parents, a recently married man with a pregnant wife, died that night.

It was also not the first time. Residents of Mgbakwu reported that a year earlier, another youth from the same community was killed by what was described as a stray bullet from the same Udogachi operatives. That death, according to protesters, received no meaningful accountability.

---

## The Protest: Bodies, Placards, and a Government House Gate

By Friday morning, the community's grief had turned to organised action.

Hundreds of youths, predominantly from Mgbakwu, marched from the community toward the Anambra State Government House, known as the Light House, in Awka. They carried the remains of Chinyeaka Ike. They carried placards. They carried green leaves, a symbol of mourning and protest rooted in Igbo tradition.

The marchers were stopped by security operatives at the Alex Ekwueme Square Gate on Emeka Anyaoku Boulevard, the approach road to the Light House. Police were stationed in numbers at the perimeter. The protesters did not reach the governor's residence, but their presence in Awka's streets sent a message that could not be contained behind a gate.

Across the city, the mood sharpened. Tension gripped Awka. Youths and women flooded the streets beyond the march itself. Protesters stormed the Anambra State Police Command headquarters and the offices of the implicated security outfits. Tyres were burned at road junctions in the Mgbakwu area. Entrances to a popular local market were blocked.

The protesters' demands were direct and unambiguous: the immediate arrest and prosecution of those responsible for Chinyeaka Ike's death. An end to the pattern of extrajudicial violence they described as recurring and unaccountable. And a personal intervention from Governor Charles Soludo.

---

## The Government's Response: Silence and Deflection

The Anambra State Government's response to the protest and to the killing has, so far, been conspicuously absent.

When SaharaReporters contacted the Commissioner for Information, Dr. Law Mefor, to seek an official reaction, he neither confirmed nor denied the killing, instead directing the journalist to the Agunaechemba Commander and Special Adviser to the Governor on Community Security, Chief Ken Emeakayi. When reached, Emeakayi requested time to respond but did not return subsequent calls.

Efforts to reach Anambra State Police Public Relations Officer SP Tochukwu Ikenga were unsuccessful.

By Saturday morning, no official statement had been issued by the state government, the police command, or the SASA unit on the circumstances of Ike's death or on the protests that followed.

That silence is its own statement. For a community that has now buried two of its sons in similar circumstances within twelve months, the absence of an official response does not read as administrative delay. It reads as institutional indifference.

---

## The Wider Pattern: Security Outfits With No Accountability

The Anambra State Special Anti-Touting Squad was created to address a real problem. Street touting, petty crime, and communal disruption in Anambra's urban areas are genuine challenges that communities have demanded action on. The unit was established as part of Governor Soludo's broader security architecture for the state.

But residents of Mgbakwu, and advocates following the pattern of incidents across Anambra, describe a unit that has evolved well beyond its original mandate. In the words of protesters and community leaders, the SASA and Udogachi operatives have "morphed into slaughter squads operating with little to no oversight."

The night-time raid on a community in pursuit of drug suspects, which resulted in the death of a man described by witnesses as uninvolved, fits a pattern that human rights observers have flagged repeatedly across Nigerian state security apparatus. When operatives are empowered to conduct armed raids with limited supervision and no immediate accountability mechanism, the risk of civilian harm is not a hypothetical. It is, as Mgbakwu has now experienced twice, a documented outcome.

The killing also lands at a particular moment in Nigeria's national conversation about security reform. Earlier the same week, a viral video from Delta State showed a police officer shooting a restrained suspect at close range, drawing widespread condemnation nationally and internationally. The two incidents, occurring days apart, have converged in public discourse as evidence of a systemic failure rather than isolated incidents.

---

## Who Was Chinyeaka Ike?

In the coverage of security crises, the individuals at the centre of them are often reduced to their circumstances. Chinyeaka Ike deserves to be named clearly.

He was 26 years old. He was the only son of his parents, a fact his community has emphasised repeatedly in describing the weight of the loss. He had recently married. His wife is expecting their first child next month.

He was known in his community as Akidi. He died on a Thursday night in the place he grew up, during a security raid that his community says he had nothing to do with.

That is who this protest is about. That is who Governor Soludo is being asked to reckon with.

---

## What Protesters Are Demanding

The demands from the Mgbakwu protest are consistent and specific:

The immediate arrest of the SASA operatives responsible for Chinyeaka Ike's death. A transparent, independent investigation into the killing, not one conducted by the same security structures being accused. A direct public statement and personal intervention from Governor Charles Soludo. An immediate review of the operational mandate and oversight framework governing SASA and Udogachi operatives. Accountability for the previous killing in Mgbakwu from a year ago that went unaddressed.

Protesters have vowed to remain on the streets until these demands receive a substantive government response.

---

## The EndSARS Echo

Anyone who lived through October 2020 will feel the shape of this moment. The pattern is familiar: a Nigerian security operative kills a civilian. The community protests. The government either deflects or stays silent. The country watches.

The EndSARS movement of 2020 began with exactly this kind of local, community-level outrage over specific, named victims. What made it national was the accumulation of incidents that could no longer be treated as isolated. Chinyeaka Ike's death is not being framed nationally in those terms yet. But the community of Mgbakwu, which has now lost two young men to the same security unit within twelve months, is not interested in how the incident is being framed nationally. They are interested in justice for one man. One family. One community.

Whether the Anambra State Government responds to that demand, or whether it waits for the streets to quiet down, will say something important about whether anything in Nigeria's relationship between security forces and the communities they are meant to protect has actually changed since 2020.

---

## Conclusion

Chinyeaka Ike is dead. His wife will give birth next month to a child who will never meet their father. His parents have lost their only son. His community has buried one of its young men for the second time in twelve months under similar circumstances.

The protest that carried his body through the streets of Awka toward a government house gate was not a security threat. It was a community demanding the most basic thing that any government owes its people: acknowledgement, accountability, and the assurance that the instruments of state power will not be allowed to kill with impunity.

Governor Soludo has built a reputation as a reform-minded administrator. This moment is a test of what that reputation means when the people asking for reform are not economists or investors. They are the parents and friends and neighbours of a 26-year-old man who should still be alive.

The streets of Awka are waiting for an answer.

*All information sourced from Sahara Reporters, Punch Newspapers, Daily Post Nigeria, Crime Focus News, and The News Chronicle. Facts presented reflect multiple eyewitness and media accounts as of 2 May 2026. The official circumstances of the killing remain subject to investigation.*
author: Century Blog Editorial Team

title: Social Media Influencers in Nigeria: How They Make Money in 2026
excerpt: How do influencers Nigeria earn real income in 2026? From brand deals to UGC contracts and social commerce, here is the complete breakdown with actual naira figures.
content:
The Nigerian influencer economy is no longer an experiment. It is a documented, growing industry worth $350 million in 2026 and expanding at 32% year-on-year. Young Nigerians who once had no blueprint for turning a smartphone and an audience into a living wage are now signing multi-million naira brand deals, launching product lines, buying property in Lekki, and building media companies from what started as a TikTok account or an Instagram page.

![Social Media Influencers in Nigeria: How They Make Money in 2026](https://res.cloudinary.com/dhmtrmwva/image/upload/v1777728080/century-blog/blog/images/social-media-influencers-in-nigeria-how-they-make-money-in-2026-6b421374-b4b0-4ca4-9231-3c221809ef53.png)

But most of the content written about this industry either tells you what worked in the United States two years ago or gives you a motivational overview without any of the numbers that actually matter.

This article is different. Every figure here is verified. Every income stream described reflects what is working in Nigeria in 2026, not what works in theory.

If you are a young Nigerian thinking about whether influencer marketing is a realistic career path, or if you are already creating and want to understand where the real money sits, read this in full.

---

## How Big Is the Nigerian Influencer Market in 2026?

The numbers set the context before anything else.

The influencer marketing market in Nigeria is valued at $350 million in 2026, growing at 32% year-on-year, making it the fastest-growing influencer market on the African continent. Nigeria leads Africa's creator economy alongside South Africa and Kenya, and 61% of Nigerian consumers trust influencer recommendations more than traditional advertising - a figure that explains why brands are shifting budget aggressively into this space.

Ad spending in Africa's influencer advertising industry will reach $206.50 million by the end of 2026, with Nigeria alone projected to reach $5.31 million, expanding at a 7.65% annual rate.

Nigeria's social commerce market hit an estimated $2.04 billion in 2025 and is growing at a 14.2% annual rate. The largest driver of that growth is creators who figured out that selling products directly to their audience pays more than any CPM rate a platform can offer.

The top platforms for influencer marketing in Nigeria are Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, and X (formerly Twitter). The top-performing niches by brand investment are entertainment, music, fashion, technology, and comedy.

---

## The Influencer Tiers: What Nigerian Creators Actually Earn

The most practical way to understand influencer income in Nigeria is through the tier system, which categorises creators by audience size and corresponds directly to what brands pay.

**Nano influencers (1,000 to 10,000 followers)**

Nano influencers are often dismissed as "too small" by people who do not understand how the industry works. In reality, this tier is where many creators begin generating their first meaningful income, and where brands increasingly find their best return on investment.

Brand deals at this tier typically range from ₦20,000 to ₦100,000 per sponsored post. Video content commands higher: ₦40,000 to ₦200,000 per branded video. A nano influencer with a highly engaged audience in a specific niche (skincare, food, tech reviews, or student life content) can earn ₦50,000 to ₦300,000 per campaign when working with brands whose product directly matches their audience.

The key insight for nano influencers: engagement rate matters more than follower count. A 5,000-follower account with 12% engagement is more valuable to most brands than a 50,000-follower account with 1.5% engagement.

**Micro influencers (10,000 to 100,000 followers)**

This tier is where consistent income becomes more reliable. Brand deals range from ₦100,000 to ₦700,000 per post depending on niche and engagement. A micro influencer running two to three brand deals per month can generate between ₦200,000 and ₦2 million monthly from brand partnerships alone.

Nigerian brands across telecoms, banking, fashion, and food and beverage have shifted significant marketing budget toward micro influencers in 2026, because the engagement is genuine, the audience trust is high, and the cost per conversion is dramatically lower than celebrity partnerships.

**Macro influencers (100,000 to 1,000,000 followers)**

At this tier, brand deals become genuinely life-changing. Sponsored posts range from ₦700,000 to ₦8 million. Video content commands ₦5 million to ₦15 million. An influencer at this level with consistent deal flow can earn tens of millions of naira annually from brand partnerships alone.

The distinction that matters at this tier: brands are no longer just paying for reach. They are paying for cultural association, audience trust, and the specific personality of the creator. This is where the difference between a transactional brand post and a genuine brand partnership becomes commercially significant.

**Celebrity mega influencers (1 million+ followers)**

At the top of the market, the numbers become difficult to separate from the broader celebrity entertainment economy. Davido, the most-followed Nigerian artist on Instagram with 31 million followers, holds endorsement partnerships with Puma, Pepsi, and Infinix among others. Burna Boy's endorsement arrangements, including Pepsi, Martell Cognac, Glo Nigeria, and Chipper Cash, are estimated to earn him between $5 million and $7 million per year from brand collaborations alone.

A single post from a Nigerian celebrity influencer at this level can cost brands between ₦500,000 and ₦5,000,000 or more, depending on the deliverable and the exclusivity terms.

---

## The Six Income Streams Nigerian Influencers Use in 2026

Understanding how Nigerian influencers make money requires understanding that the most successful ones never rely on a single source. The top earners stack multiple income streams deliberately, building incomes that survive algorithm changes and platform policy shifts.

### 1. Brand Deals and Sponsored Content

This is the primary income stream for most Nigerian influencers across all tiers. Brands in Nigeria and internationally pay creators to feature products and services in their content, either as standalone sponsored posts, integrated mentions within organic content, or long-term ambassadorship arrangements.

The most lucrative sectors for Nigerian influencer brand deals in 2026 are: telecoms (MTN, Airtel, Glo, T2 Mobile), banking and fintech (Opay, Moniepoint, Flutterwave, Kuda), food and beverage (including international brands entering the Nigerian market), beauty and fashion, and increasingly, betting and gaming companies.

Long-term ambassadorship deals, in which a creator becomes the face of a brand for six to twelve months, consistently pay more per deliverable than individual post rates and provide income stability that one-off deals cannot.

### 2. User-Generated Content (UGC) Creation

This is the most underrated and most misunderstood income stream in the Nigerian influencer market in 2026. UGC creation means producing content for brands that the brand then uses in their own marketing, not the creator's channel. You do not need a large following to do it. You need a decent camera, good lighting, and the ability to make authentic, relatable video content.

Beginners earn $50 to $150 per UGC video. Experienced UGC creators charge $300 to $500 per video and above. Platforms including Collabstr, Diglancers, and JoinBrands actively connect Nigerian UGC creators with paying brands. Fintech companies such as Flutterwave, Chipper Cash, and Afriex are particularly active in hiring Nigerian UGC creators because they need content that feels culturally authentic to Nigerian consumers.

The one genuine challenge worth noting: AI-generated UGC tools have pushed average deliverable costs down 44% year-on-year. The competitive edge for Nigerian creators is the authenticity and cultural specificity that no AI tool can replicate. A brand selling to Nigerian consumers cannot reproduce the cultural nuance of a real Nigerian creator explaining why a product fits their daily life.

### 3. Affiliate Marketing and Social Commerce

Nigeria's social commerce market at $2.04 billion is being driven primarily by creators who earn commissions on every sale they generate for a brand. Affiliate marketing in Nigeria has matured significantly: local programmes through Jumia, Konga, and major Nigerian banks sit alongside international programmes through Amazon and AliExpress.

The appeal of affiliate income is its scalability. Unlike brand deals, which pay a fixed fee regardless of results, affiliate commissions grow with the creator's influence over purchasing decisions. A creator whose audience trusts their product recommendations can earn affiliate income that significantly outpaces their sponsored post rates.

WhatsApp commerce deserves specific mention here. Many Nigerian influencers use WhatsApp broadcast lists to sell products directly to their most loyal audience members, bypassing every platform algorithm entirely. This direct-to-audience commerce model generates income that no platform policy change can affect.

### 4. Platform Monetisation

This is where the most important honest warning in this article lives. TikTok's Creator Rewards Programme does not pay a single creator in Sub-Saharan Africa. Instagram's native payouts are so inconsistent they barely register as meaningful income for most Nigerian creators.

YouTube AdSense remains the most reliable platform income for Nigerian creators, but the regional ad rates are significantly lower than Western markets. A Nigerian channel generating the same views as a US-based channel will earn a fraction of the AdSense revenue.

What actually works: YouTube monetisation for channels with significant international viewership, Facebook monetisation for creators whose content reaches diaspora audiences with higher CPMs, and X (formerly Twitter) ad revenue sharing for verified accounts with strong engagement.

### 5. Live Streaming and Digital Events

TikTok Live gifting, YouTube Live super chats, and Facebook Live donations have created a real-time income stream for Nigerian creators who build genuinely engaged audiences. Peller, one of Nigeria's highest-earning TikTok creators, reportedly earned $30,000 in a single live session from viewer gifts alone.

Beyond platform gifting, many established Nigerian influencers run paid virtual events, masterclasses, and webinars at ₦5,000 to ₦50,000 per ticket. A creator with 50,000 engaged followers selling 200 tickets to a paid masterclass generates ₦1 million to ₦10 million per event, with minimal platform dependency.

### 6. Product Launches, Investments, and Business Ownership

The most financially sophisticated Nigerian influencers in 2026 have used their platforms as launchpads for independent businesses. Skincare lines, apparel brands, food products, and production studios are all examples of businesses built on the foundation of an existing audience.

This transition from creator to business owner is the most reliable path to the kind of wealth that survives beyond the lifecycle of any single social media platform. The audience trust built through years of content creation becomes the most powerful marketing channel for any product the creator chooses to launch.

---

## The Platforms: Where Nigerian Influencers Are Building in 2026

**Instagram** remains the primary platform for brand deal conversations and relationship building. It is not a reliable direct-pay platform for Nigerian creators, but it is where brand deals are negotiated and closed. Nano to macro influencers use Instagram primarily as a deal-closing and audience relationship tool.

**TikTok** is the fastest-growth platform for Nigerian creators in 2026. Despite not paying through its Creator Fund in Nigeria, TikTok drives brand deal enquiries, merchandise sales, and live gifting income at rates that make it essential for any creator targeting the under-30 audience.

**YouTube** provides the most sustainable long-term platform income for Nigerian creators, particularly those who build content with international reach. The combination of AdSense, Super Chats, memberships, and affiliate integration makes YouTube the most financially complete platform available to Nigerian creators.

**X (formerly Twitter)** has unusual prominence in the Nigerian influencer market compared to other African markets. Brand deal conversations, cultural commentary, and news breaking happen on X in ways that give creators genuine leverage for sponsored partnerships, particularly in finance, tech, and entertainment.

---

## What the Tax Reality Means for Nigerian Influencer Income

The Nigeria Tax Act 2025, which took effect from January 2026, formally treats all influencer income as taxable. This includes brand deal payments, affiliate commissions, platform ad revenue, and even the commercial value of free products received from brands as part of partnerships.

Creators earning above approximately ₦800,000 annually after basic relief adjustments are subject to progressive personal income tax. Lagos-based creators have already felt this directly: TikTok star Peller received a ₦36 million tax demand earlier in 2026, creating significant public conversation about how influencer income is assessed and calculated.

Any creator building a serious income from influence in 2026 needs to: open a dedicated business account for creator income, work with an accountant who understands the digital creator space, and keep detailed records of all income sources including foreign platform payments.

Foreign income, particularly dollar-denominated payments from international brands or platforms, requires specific account infrastructure. Grey and Raenest (formerly Geegpay) are the two most widely used tools among Nigerian creators receiving foreign currency payments, offering virtual USD, GBP, and EUR accounts with competitive conversion rates.

---

## Common Mistakes Young Nigerian Influencers Make

**Chasing follower count instead of engagement quality.** Brands in 2026 use AI and data tools to verify engagement authenticity before signing any deal. Bought followers are immediately visible in analytics and will disqualify a creator from serious brand partnerships.

**Relying on a single platform.** Every platform has changed its algorithm, payment structure, or policy terms significantly at least once in the past three years. Creators who built everything on TikTok alone were affected by Creator Fund changes. Those who built an email list or WhatsApp community alongside their main platform were not.

**Not charging their worth.** Many Nigerian nano and micro influencers undercharge for brand deals because they do not have access to benchmark rate information. The figures in this article are those benchmarks. Know the range before you negotiate.

**Treating influencer income as informal.** The tax demand Peller received was not exceptional. As the industry grows and generates documented revenue, FIRS and state tax authorities are increasingly paying attention. Treating influencer income as informal and undocumented is a risk that grows with every naira earned.

**Posting without a strategy.** The Nigerian influencers building sustainable careers in 2026 treat their content like a business: with a content calendar, analytics review, reinvestment plan, and a clear understanding of which content types drive brand enquiries versus which types build audience.

---

## Practical First Steps for Young Nigerians Who Want to Start

Pick one niche and one primary platform. Create consistently for 90 days before evaluating results. Build your audience authentically before approaching brands. Use free tools: CapCut for video editing, Canva for graphics, and a simple Google Sheet for tracking content performance and brand deal enquiries.

When your engagement is strong and consistent, approach local brands in your niche directly. A well-written pitch email with your engagement rate, audience demographics, and a simple content proposal is enough to open conversations at the nano and micro level.

Build a WhatsApp broadcast list from the start. It is the most direct, algorithm-proof connection to your audience that you can build for free.

And finally: understand that the Nigerian influencer economy rewards the patient. The creators who are earning significant money in 2026 started two, three, or four years ago and kept going when nothing was happening yet. Consistency is the competitive advantage that cannot be bought.

┌──────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Income Stream            │ Earnings Potential (Nigeria 2026)    │
├──────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Brand Deals              │ ₦20k (nano) to ₦15M+ (macro) per job│
│ UGC Creation             │ $50 to $500+ per video               │
│ Affiliate / Commerce     │ % per sale, scales with audience     │
│ Platform Monetisation    │ YouTube best; TikTok Fund = ₦0 in NG │
│ Live Streaming & Events  │ ₦0 to $30,000 per session            │
│ Products & Investments   │ Unlimited ceiling; audience-dependent│
└──────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────┘

---

## Conclusion

The Nigerian influencer economy in 2026 is real, documented, and growing faster than almost any other sector in the country's digital landscape. The income is real. The brand deals are real. The tax obligations are real.

What separates the creators building lasting careers from those who burn out after a few viral moments is not talent. It is strategy, consistency, and the business literacy to understand what they are building before they need to protect it.

The market is not saturated. The opportunity has never been more structured. And with 63% of Nigerians under 25 and a social media penetration rate that continues to climb, the audience waiting to discover the next generation of Nigerian influencers is larger than it has ever been.

Your phone is in your pocket. Your niche exists. The only variable left is whether you start.

*Income figures sourced from TIMA Agency, ConnectNigeria, Snippet Influencer Rates, Albanny Technologies, and Gistreel. Tax information sourced from the Nigeria Tax Act 2025. Market valuation sourced from Pandora Agency analysis. All figures correct as of May 2026.*

title: Champions League Highlights and Predictions: Semi-Finals Preview (May 2026)
excerpt: Full Champions League predictions and highlights for the 2026 semi-finals. Arsenal vs Atlético and Bayern vs PSG previewed with live data, key stats, and match analysis.
content:
The 2025-26 UEFA Champions League has produced one of the most dramatic knockout rounds in recent memory. Real Madrid eliminated. Barcelona eliminated. Liverpool dispatched in three matches by PSG without scoring a single goal. And at the centre of it all, an Arsenal side that has gone eight matches unbeaten in this competition, dropping zero points from the group stage and marching into the semi-finals with a composure that no previous version of this club has managed at this level.

![Champions League Highlights and Predictions: Semi-Finals Preview (May 2026)](https://res.cloudinary.com/dhmtrmwva/image/upload/v1777727542/century-blog/blog/images/champions-league-highlights-and-predictions-semi-finals-preview-may-2026-883c1708-8ab9-4683-9e9c-fc922e23ab5f.png)

Two semi-final ties now stand between the four remaining clubs and the final at Munich's Allianz Arena on 30 May 2026. Arsenal host Atlético Madrid at the Emirates on Tuesday 5 May. Bayern Munich host Paris Saint-Germain at the Allianz Arena on Wednesday 6 May. Both second legs follow the week after.

Here is everything you need to know: the highlights that shaped the semi-finals, the numbers behind each club, and predictions for how these ties will unfold.

---

## The Road to the Semi-Finals: Key Results That Defined the Tournament

### Arsenal: Flawless and Relentless

Arsenal have been the standout team of this Champions League campaign. Their record across eight matches reads: eight wins, zero draws, zero losses, 24 points - a perfect group stage by any measure.

The quarter-final against Atlético Madrid is now at the semi-final stage, with the first leg ending 1-1 in Madrid on 29 April. Arsenal's away goal at the Metropolitano came via a composed finish that silenced one of European football's most hostile atmospheres. Atlético pulled level before the end, setting up an Emirates second leg in which Arsenal carry the slight advantage of home ground and a 58.3% win probability.

Before that, Arsenal dispatched Sporting CP across two legs: a 1-0 win in Lisbon on 7 April and a goalless draw at the Emirates on 15 April - enough to advance. It was the kind of disciplined, defensively sound progression that Mikel Arteta's side has made their signature in this competition.

### Bayern Munich: The Team That Eliminated Real Madrid

The most dramatic result of the quarter-finals belonged to Bayern Munich. Real Madrid, the tournament's most decorated club and holders of the last four Champions League trophies across six years, were eliminated in a tie of extraordinary goals.

Real Madrid won the first leg at the Bernabéu 2-1 on 7 April. Bayern then produced one of the performances of the tournament, winning 4-3 at the Allianz Arena on 15 April to advance 5-4 on aggregate. In a match that swung repeatedly and featured seven goals across 90 minutes, Bayern's clinical finishing and high defensive line eventually proved decisive. The Allianz Arena at full voice in a must-win European night delivered exactly the kind of spectacle the Champions League exists to produce.

Bayern now sit second in the overall standings on 21 points from eight matches: seven wins, one loss.

### PSG: Dominant, Clinical, and Three Goals Better Than Liverpool Across 180 Minutes

Paris Saint-Germain's quarter-final against Liverpool produced one of the starkest results of the round. PSG won 2-0 in Paris on 8 April. PSG won 2-0 at Anfield on 14 April. Four goals, none conceded, across two matches against one of England's most feared European sides.

What makes PSG's performance even more striking is the manner of the victories. Liverpool were not simply outscored. They were outplayed, their high press neutralised, their attacking transitions cut off, and their set-piece threat contained. PSG's defensive structure under Luis Enrique has become as impressive as their attacking efficiency.

PSG enter the semi-final against Bayern on 23 points from their overall campaign: four wins, two losses, two draws - a record that places them 11th in the overall standings. But knockout football operates on different logic. The team that won 2-0 twice against Liverpool is a different proposition to the one that stumbled in the group stage.

### Atlético Madrid: From Barcelona Elimination to Semi-Final

Atlético Madrid's quarter-final against Barcelona produced one of the ties of the tournament. Atlético won 2-0 at the Camp Nou on 8 April. Barcelona won 2-1 at the Metropolitano on 14 April. Atlético advanced 3-2 on aggregate, eliminating Barcelona in a tie defined by tactical chess, key moments from Ademola Lookman on the Atlético side, and a Barcelona implosion in the first leg that they never fully recovered from.

Atlético's overall record stands at four wins, three losses, one draw for 13 points - lower than their semi-final appearance might suggest, reflecting an inconsistent group stage followed by exceptional knockout form. This is an Atlético side that peaks when elimination is on the table.

---

## Semi-Final Preview 1: Arsenal vs Atlético Madrid

**First leg result:** Atlético 1-1 Arsenal (29 April, Madrid)
**Second leg:** Arsenal vs Atlético, Tuesday 5 May, Emirates Stadium, 8 PM WAT
**Win probability (second leg):** Arsenal 58.3% | Draw 23.8% | Atlético 17.9%

Arsenal hold the narrow advantage. The away goal at the Metropolitano means Atlético must score at the Emirates if they are to advance. A 0-0 draw sends Arsenal through. Any Arsenal goal means Atlético need at least two.

The Emirates in a Champions League semi-final is a fixture that this generation of Arsenal supporters has not experienced before. The atmosphere will be extraordinary. The question is whether the occasion lifts the team or tightens them.

**What Arsenal need to do:** Control possession, press high, and use the width. Atlético's defensive block is compact and difficult to break down centrally. Arsenal's best route to goal runs through the flanks and into the channels behind Atlético's aggressive pressing line.

**What Atlético need to do:** Score first. If Arsenal concede early at the Emirates, the match becomes significantly more open and Atlético's counter-attacking transitions, the most dangerous weapon in Diego Simeone's tactical arsenal, become exponentially more threatening.

**Key player to watch (Arsenal):** Martin Ødegaard. The Norwegian midfielder controls the tempo of every Arsenal move and his ability to find pockets of space in tight defensive systems is what separates Arsenal's build-up from simply recycling possession.

**Key player to watch (Atlético):** Ademola Lookman. The Nigerian forward has been exceptional since joining in January 2026, scoring key goals in the Barcelona tie including a strike at the Camp Nou that effectively ended the first leg as a contest. A player in this form, against former club territory, in a semi-final, is exactly the kind of variable that changes matches.

**Prediction:** Arsenal 2-0 Atlético Madrid (Arsenal advance 3-1 on aggregate). The Emirates crowd, the pressure on Atlético to attack, and Arsenal's superior recent form collectively favour the home side. If Atlético score first, all bets are off. But Arsenal's defensive record in this tournament is exceptional, and Arteta will set up to exploit the space Atlético must leave when chasing the game.

---

## Semi-Final Preview 2: Bayern Munich vs PSG

**First leg result:** PSG 5-4 Bayern Munich (28 April, Paris)
**Second leg:** Bayern Munich vs PSG, Wednesday 6 May, Allianz Arena, 8 PM WAT
**Win probability (second leg):** Bayern 57.3% | Draw 19.2% | PSG 23.5%

This tie has already produced nine goals in the first leg. PSG won 5-4 in a match at the Parc des Princes that was as chaotic as the scoreline suggests. Bayern now need to win by two or more goals at the Allianz Arena to advance. Win by one and the tie goes to extra time. Win by exactly two and it goes to extra time and potentially penalties.

PSG only need a 1-1 draw at the Allianz Arena to reach the final. That defensive posture suits Luis Enrique's team enormously, given how well they contained Liverpool in the quarter-final.

**What Bayern need to do:** Replicate their 4-3 home performance against Real Madrid. The Allianz Arena in must-win mode, with the support fully behind the team, is an environment Bayern have exploited repeatedly this season. They need a fast start, ideally a goal within the first 20 minutes, to shift the tie's psychological balance.

**What PSG need to do:** Score on the counter. The pattern of this tie, and of PSG's European campaign generally, involves absorbing pressure and striking on the transition. If Bayern chase the game and leave space in behind, PSG are exactly the team to punish it. One away goal changes everything.

**Key player to watch (Bayern):** Harry Kane. The England captain has been one of the most consistent centre-forwards in Europe this season. In a match where Bayern need goals, Kane's combination of clinical finishing, hold-up play, and movement in the box is what their attacking system revolves around.

**Key player to watch (PSG):** Ousmane Dembélé. The French winger's direct running, pace in transition, and ability to create chances from nothing are perfectly suited to PSG's counter-attacking brief in this second leg. If the Allianz Arena opens up as Bayern push for goals, Dembélé will be the most dangerous player on the pitch.

**Prediction:** Bayern Munich 3-1 PSG (tie level at 7-7 on aggregate, goes to extra time and penalties). This is the more genuinely unpredictable of the two ties. A Bayern win on the night feels likely given home advantage and the Allianz Arena atmosphere in an elimination match. But PSG's ability to score on the counter makes a clean sheet an unrealistic expectation. The scenario that feels most probable: a high-scoring Bayern win that takes the tie to extra time, with penalties as the ultimate decider.

**Penalty shootout call:** Bayern Munich advance. Their experience in knockout football, their home support, and Kane's ice-cold record from the spot collectively tip the balance.

---

## The Overall Picture: Who Lifts the Trophy in Munich?

If the predictions above hold, the Champions League final on 30 May at the Allianz Arena will feature Arsenal against Bayern Munich - an all-English versus German final in a stadium that Bayern call home.

The irony of Bayern potentially playing a European final at their own ground is not lost on anyone. But finals are determined on the night, not by geography.

**Arsenal's case for the trophy:** They are the only team in this tournament with a perfect record from the group stage. They have won eight matches and lost none. Their defensive structure is elite, their pressing is organised, and Arteta has built a squad with genuine depth at every position. A team that has not dropped a point in eight European matches has earned the right to be called favourites.

**Bayern's case for the trophy:** They have eliminated the tournament's most decorated club. Their home support in a final at the Allianz Arena would be overwhelming. And a team that scored four against Real Madrid and could score three or more against PSG in the second leg is a team in extraordinary attacking form at exactly the right moment of the season.

**The wildcard:** If PSG produce an upset at the Allianz Arena and advance, the final becomes a genuinely different conversation. PSG have shown they can eliminate elite opponents. A PSG vs Arsenal final would pit the most free-scoring team in the knockout rounds against the most defensively solid.

---

## Champions League Standings: Full Picture

For context, here is where the four remaining clubs sit in the overall tournament standings after the group stage:

| Rank | Club | W | D | L | Points |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1st | Arsenal | 8 | 0 | 0 | 24 |
| 2nd | Bayern Munich | 7 | 0 | 1 | 21 |
| 11th | PSG | 4 | 2 | 2 | 14 |
| 14th | Atlético Madrid | 4 | 1 | 3 | 13 |

The standings tell a clear story: Arsenal and Bayern are the competition's two dominant forces by record. PSG and Atlético are knockout specialists who have outperformed their group stage records when elimination was on the table.

---

## Conclusion

The 2025-26 Champions League semi-finals offer two distinct stories. Arsenal vs Atlético is the tie of defensive discipline versus counter-attacking threat, with a slight but meaningful advantage to the home side. Bayern vs PSG is nine goals in the first leg and the promise of more to come, a tactical battle that could end anywhere from a routine Bayern win to a PSG upset for the ages.

What is not in doubt is the quality. These are four of the most compelling clubs in European football, each with the capacity to win a Champions League trophy. Two of them will be eliminated next week.

The final in Munich on 30 May cannot come soon enough.

*All match results, standings, and win probabilities sourced from live UEFA Champions League data as of 1 May 2026. Figures correct at time of publication.*

title: Nigerian Comedy Industry: Growth, Opportunities, and What Creators Need to Know in 2026
excerpt: The comedy industry Nigeria is building in 2026 is worth over $31 million and employs over one million people. Here is what every creator needs to understand about the opportunity.
content:
What started as young Nigerians recording short videos on affordable smartphones and uploading them to Instagram has become one of the most significant creative economies the country has ever produced.

![Nigerian Comedy Industry: Growth, Opportunities, and What Creators Need to Know in 2026](https://res.cloudinary.com/dhmtrmwva/image/upload/v1777677415/century-blog/blog/images/nigerian-comedy-industry-growth-opportunities-and-what-creators-need-to-know-in-2026-3306ee10-ec45-49d4-a3e6-eb23dcb3b809.png)

Nigerian comedy, specifically the short-form skit economy, has in a few short years joined Afrobeats and Nollywood as a recognised pillar of the country's global cultural export. It has created millionaires, employed hundreds of thousands, attracted brand investment worth hundreds of millions of naira annually, and put Nigerian humour on feeds in countries that had never previously thought about Nigeria at all.

For creators thinking about whether there is still space to build something meaningful in this industry, the answer in 2026 is a clear yes. But the landscape has also matured, and entering it today requires a different strategy than it did five years ago.

This is a full breakdown of how the Nigerian comedy industry got here, where the real opportunities lie in 2026, and what separates the creators who are building lasting careers from those who burn out after a few viral moments.

---

## The Numbers Behind the Skit Economy

Before examining strategy, the scale of what has been built deserves attention.

Skit-making is now estimated to be Nigeria's third largest entertainment industry sector, with a net worth of over $31 million. The Nigerian entertainment industry as a whole is rated as the second most significant employer of youths in the country after agriculture, employing over one million people directly and indirectly. Two-thirds of Nigerians watch comedy skits frequently, according to research cited in the 2024 book Skit Economy, which chronicles the industry's rise in detail.

These are not niche figures. They reflect a genuine mass-market industry that has emerged almost entirely through the ingenuity of young creators operating with minimal infrastructure support from either government or established institutions.

The demographic conditions driving this growth are equally significant. With 63% of Nigerians under the age of 25 and among the highest social media engagement rates in Africa, the country presents an almost uniquely favourable environment for digital comedy. The audience is young, mobile-first, socially connected, and hungry for content that reflects their actual lived experience. Nigerian skit-makers understood this before brands did, and they moved accordingly.

---

## How the Industry Got Here

Nigerian comedy has a longer history than the skit era suggests. Ali Baba, known as the Godfather of Nigerian Comedy, spent over 30 years building comedy into a respected profession before the internet changed the distribution model entirely. Basketmouth, who today earns over ₦360 million annually from his shows, helped establish international touring as a viable income stream for Nigerian comedians through venues like the Indigo at the O2 in London.

The digital pivot came in the early 2010s, when Mark Angel Comedy became the first African comedy channel to reach one million YouTube subscribers. The formula was simple: short, family-friendly skits featuring recognisable everyday Nigerian scenarios, anchored by the child comedian Emmanuella, whose expressiveness transcended language and cultural barriers. Mark Angel Comedy now generates hundreds of thousands of dollars annually from YouTube AdSense alone.

What Mark Angel proved, and what the generation that followed him built on, was that Nigerian humour was inherently shareable. The cultural specificity that might seem like a limitation, the Lagos references, the Yoruba code-switching, the recognisable parenting archetypes, was actually the asset. Audiences around the world found Nigerian skits through the specificity, not despite it.

Broda Shaggi, Sabinus (Mr. Funny), Taaooma, Mr. Macaroni, Cute Abiola, and Brain Jotter represent the generation that took Mark Angel's blueprint and scaled it across multiple platforms simultaneously, building audiences on Instagram, YouTube, TikTok, and Facebook in parallel rather than relying on any single platform.

---

## The Money: How Nigerian Comedians Are Earning in 2026

Understanding how money flows through the Nigerian comedy industry is essential for any creator thinking about building a sustainable career within it.

**Brand endorsements** remain the highest-value income stream for established creators. Nigerian companies, including telecoms, banks, food and beverage brands, and consumer goods companies, now budget significant sums specifically for skit-maker partnerships. The appeal is direct: skit-makers deliver engaged, loyal audiences at a cost per impression that traditional media cannot match. Top creators command fees that would have been unimaginable for a social media personality five years ago.

**Platform monetisation** has grown as a meaningful income source, though it comes with important caveats. YouTube AdSense pays significantly less per view in Nigeria than in Western markets due to lower regional advertising rates. A channel earning $10,000 per month from a primarily US audience might earn $1,500 from the same view count with a Nigerian audience. Creators who optimise for global viewership, not just local virality, capture significantly higher platform revenue.

**Live shows and appearances** have evolved beyond the traditional stand-up format. Sabinus, whose "investor" character became one of the most recognised comedy personalities in Nigeria, has successfully transitioned from purely digital content to hosting sold-out stadium shows. This crossover from screen to stage is increasingly the mark of a creator who has built a brand rather than just an audience. Booking fees for major skit-makers at corporate events, weddings, and entertainment shows can reach seven figures per appearance.

**Merchandise, IP licensing, and media production** represent the frontier for creators who think beyond the skit format. Basketmouth produces successful web series including Papa Benji and My Flatmates. Taaooma has leveraged her multi-character skit format into acting roles and brand consultancy. Mr. Macaroni combines his comedy platform with social activism, which has expanded his brand beyond pure entertainment into a cultural voice that commands different kinds of partnership.

**A note on taxation:** The Nigeria Tax Act 2025, which took effect from January 2026, now formally treats content creator income as taxable. This includes AdSense revenue, brand deals, sponsored content, and even the value of free products received from sponsors. Creators earning above approximately ₦800,000 annually after basic relief adjustments will pay progressive personal income tax. This is not optional and it is not new for Lagos-based creators, some of whom have already received significant demands from the Lagos Internal Revenue Service. Any creator building a serious income from comedy in 2026 should factor tax compliance into their business model from the start.

---

## The Real Opportunities in 2026

The Nigerian comedy industry in 2026 is not saturated. It is maturing. The distinction matters significantly for how a new creator should think about entering it.

**Underserved niches within comedy.** The dominant skit format is highly competitive. But specific niches within comedy remain relatively open: parenting-focused content in northern Nigerian languages, professional satire targeting Nigeria's growing tech and startup ecosystem, sports comedy tied to the Premier League's Nigerian fanbase, and sketch comedy that moves between English and Igbo or Hausa without defaulting entirely to pidgin. Creators who occupy a specific lane own it more completely than those who compete in the broad Nigerian humour middle ground.

**Long-form content.** The skit format has an attention ceiling. As creators mature and audiences age with them, demand for longer-form comedy content, extended YouTube videos, podcast comedy, and even scripted web series, is growing. Basketmouth's international touring career and Bovi's stand-up specials, including Bovi: Man on Fire, demonstrate that Nigerian comedy audiences will invest time in longer formats if the quality is there. The production bar is rising, but so is the reward for clearing it.

**The diaspora audience.** Nigerian communities in the United Kingdom, the United States, and Canada represent an audience that is currently underserved by Nigerian comedy content that speaks specifically to their experience. The IJGB (I Just Got Back) character, navigating the space between Nigerian culture and Western life, is a rich creative territory that creators living the experience have an authentic advantage in. Diaspora-focused comedy also commands significantly higher platform ad rates, which solves the regional CPM problem.

**Comedy as a gateway to other entertainment verticals.** Short-form comedy is increasingly functioning as a top-of-funnel awareness channel for Nigerian entertainers who want to build careers across music, film, and television. Several Nigerian musicians have built audiences through comedy skits before releasing music. The comedy platform establishes the personality and the audience before the product arrives. For creators with ambitions beyond pure comedy, this pathway is worth understanding deliberately.

---

## The Challenges Every Creator Must Understand

Honest advice about the Nigerian comedy industry cannot skip the structural challenges that affect even the most talented creators.

**The distribution problem.** YouTube's regional ad rates mean that a primarily Nigerian audience generates significantly less revenue per view than an international one. Creators who want platform revenue to be a sustainable income pillar need to either build international viewership deliberately or diversify aggressively into brand deals and live revenue.

**Infrastructure costs.** Producing high-quality skit content from Nigeria requires reliable electricity, fast internet, and professional production tools. These are not reliably cheap or available. Top creators invest in diesel generators, high-speed internet subscriptions, and professional cameras and lighting. These costs are real business expenses and need to be treated as such.

**Intellectual property protection.** Piracy and unauthorised reuse of Nigerian comedy content remains a serious problem. Skit ideas are copied, videos are reuploaded without credit, and monetisation is diverted away from original creators with little recourse. This is an industry-level problem without a simple individual solution, but creators who watermark their content consistently and build direct audience relationships, through newsletters, WhatsApp communities, or exclusive platforms, create some protection against the worst of it.

**Consistency as a competitive advantage.** The Nigerian comedy space rewards consistency above almost everything else. Algorithms on YouTube, Instagram, and TikTok all favour creators who publish regularly and maintain audience engagement between uploads. Creators who treat their channel as a business, with a content calendar, a production schedule, and a reinvestment plan, consistently outperform those who create when inspiration strikes.

---

## What Separates Sustainable Careers From Viral Moments

The Nigerian comedy industry has produced hundreds of viral moments and a much smaller number of sustainable careers. Understanding the difference is the most important thing any creator can take from studying the industry.

Sustainable careers in Nigerian comedy share three characteristics: a clearly defined creative identity that does not change with every trending topic, a business model that includes at least two or three income streams beyond platform ads, and a direct relationship with an audience that survives algorithm changes and platform policy shifts.

Sabinus's "investor" character is a useful example. The character is specific, immediately recognisable, and can be placed in any scenario while remaining true to its comedic logic. That specificity is what allowed Sabinus to transition from digital virality to stadium shows. The character built a brand; the brand built a business.

The creators who are one viral skit away from irrelevance are those who have not yet answered the question: what will people know me for in five years, even if they cannot remember the name of the specific video that introduced us?

---

## Expert Tips for Creators Entering the Comedy Industry in 2026

**Define your character or angle before your platform.** The strongest Nigerian comedy brands are built around a specific perspective or recurring character, not a content format. Know what you represent before you decide where you will represent it.

**Treat production quality as a competitive advantage.** The production bar for Nigerian comedy has risen significantly. A smartphone and good lighting remain viable, but poor audio quality, shaky footage, and careless editing now signal low effort to audiences who have been trained by years of increasingly professional content.

**Build your email list or community channel from day one.** Platform algorithms change. Community relationships do not. A WhatsApp broadcast list, a Telegram channel, or even a simple email newsletter creates a direct line to your audience that no platform policy can remove.

**Understand the business before you need to.** Many Nigerian creators discover the financial and legal complexity of their industry only after they have already made significant income. Tax obligations, contract terms for brand deals, and platform revenue sharing structures are all worth understanding before they become problems.

**Collaborate deliberately, not reactively.** Collaboration between Nigerian comedy creators consistently generates audience growth for both parties. The most effective collaborations connect creators whose audiences overlap but do not fully intersect. Treat collaboration as a strategic business decision, not just a creative one.

---

## Conclusion

The Nigerian comedy industry in 2026 is one of the most dynamic creative economies on the African continent. It has produced genuine wealth, global recognition, and a generation of creators who have demonstrated that talent combined with digital infrastructure can build something that matters.

The opportunity for new creators is real. The space is not saturated. But the era when a single viral video was enough to build a career has passed. What the industry rewards now is specificity, consistency, business literacy, and the patience to build something that lasts longer than an algorithm cycle.

The Nigerians who found the funny in their own experience and shared it with the world built an industry worth $31 million. The next generation of creators will build on that foundation. The only question is whether they build deliberately enough to benefit from what they create.

*Industry figures sourced from The Conversation, Global Bar Magazine, NigeriaMag, and Business Hallmark. Tax information sourced from the Nigeria Tax Act 2025. All data correct as of May 2026.*

title: Top Netflix Shows Nigerians Are Watching in 2026 (Updated May)
excerpt: Discover what is trending on Netflix Nigeria right now in 2026. From global hits to Nollywood originals, here is your complete updated watchlist for May.
content:
If you have spent the last twenty minutes scrolling through Netflix trying to decide what to watch, you are not alone. The platform adds new titles almost every week, and the Nigerian Top 10 is a constantly shifting blend of international blockbusters, Nollywood originals, and the occasional viral sensation that nobody saw coming.

![Top Netflix Shows Nigerians Are Watching in 2026 (Updated May)](https://res.cloudinary.com/dhmtrmwva/image/upload/v1777676537/century-blog/blog/images/top-netflix-shows-nigerians-are-watching-in-2026-updated-may-5e6dbac9-8d81-4e83-9fc3-1ae072627450.png)

The good news is that the Netflix Nigeria trending list in 2026 is genuinely worth paying attention to. Whether you are in the mood for a psychologically unsettling British thriller, a record-breaking Nollywood comedy, a high-octane action film starring one of Hollywood's most versatile actresses, or a Nollywood crime saga filmed in the streets of Lagos, the current charts are delivering across every genre.

This is your updated guide to what Nigerians are watching on Netflix right now, why each title is worth your time, and what makes this particular moment in streaming particularly interesting for Nigerian viewers.

---

## What Is Trending on Netflix Nigeria Right Now

### 1. Unchosen (British Psychological Thriller Series)

The title everyone in the group chat is talking about right now is Unchosen, a six-part British psychological thriller that debuted at number one on Netflix globally in the week of 20 to 26 April 2026, accumulating 10.4 million views in its first six days after its 21 April premiere.

The series has landed in the Netflix Top 10 in 69 countries simultaneously, including Nigeria, the United Kingdom, the United States, Australia, Germany, and Brazil, making it one of the most globally distributed debut performances for a British scripted series in recent years.

**What it is about:** Rosie (played by BAFTA winner Molly Windsor) lives inside a conservative Christian sect, her entire world controlled by the community's strict rules and her own compliance. A chance encounter with an escaped convict named Sam (Fra Fee) begins to crack open the life she has accepted as normal and sets her on a dangerous, personal journey toward freedom.

**Why Nigerians are watching:** The series taps into themes of faith, community control, and the courage required to question what you have always been told. These themes resonate across Nigerian audiences regardless of religious background. The pacing is tight and the twists arrive consistently enough to make binge-watching feel involuntary rather than deliberate.

**Cast:** Molly Windsor, Asa Butterfield (Sex Education), Fra Fee (Hawkeye), Christopher Eccleston, Siobhan Finneran.

**Available now on Netflix.**

---

### 2. Apex (Action Thriller Film)

While Unchosen is dominating the TV charts, Apex is doing something similar on the film side. The action thriller debuted at number one globally with 38.2 million views in its first three days, making it the third-largest Netflix film premiere of 2026 so far, behind only The Rip and War Machine.

**What it is about:** Sasha (Charlize Theron), a bereaved rock climber visiting the Blue Mountains of Australia, discovers that the most dangerous thing in the wilderness is not the terrain. It is Ben (Taron Egerton), a deranged serial killer who lures her into a cat-and-mouse hunt with no clear way out.

**Why Nigerians are watching:** Action thrillers with strong female leads consistently perform well on Netflix Nigeria, and Charlize Theron's credibility in this space, established by films like Mad Max and Atomic Blonde, brings a built-in audience. The film is relentless, visually striking, and moves fast enough to hold attention across two hours. Theron reportedly performed many of her own climbing scenes, which adds a layer of authenticity the trailer alone cannot fully convey.

**Cast:** Charlize Theron, Taron Egerton.

**Available now on Netflix.**

---

### 3. Running Point Season 2 (Sports Comedy Series)

Running Point, the Kate Hudson-led basketball comedy that became one of Netflix's surprise hits of early 2026, returned with its second season to immediate demand, debuting at number two globally with 5.3 million views in its first four days.

**What it is about:** Kate Hudson plays Isla Gordon, a woman thrust into running a professional basketball franchise she was not supposed to inherit. Season two picks up with the franchise mid-transition, the players increasingly demanding, and Isla discovering that managing people is significantly harder than managing expectations.

**Why Nigerians are watching:** The combination of workplace comedy, family dynamics, and sports-world drama has broad appeal. The show is sharp and funny without being cynical, and its short episodes (most run under 35 minutes) make it exceptionally well-suited for the kind of "just one more" viewing that defines binge culture.

**Cast:** Kate Hudson, Brenda Song, Drew Tarver.

**Available now on Netflix.**

---

### 4. Behind the Scenes (Nollywood Film)

The biggest Nollywood story on Netflix Nigeria in 2026 is not a new international acquisition. It is a domestic record-breaker. Behind the Scenes, co-directed by Funke Akindele and Tunde Olaoye, holds the record for the highest-grossing Nollywood film of all time, and it is now streaming on Netflix after its extraordinary theatrical run.

**What it is about:** Aderonke "Ronky-feller" Faniran (Scarlet Gomez) is a wealthy, generous real estate mogul who has always given freely to everyone around her. When she reaches a breaking point after years of her family's dependence on her generosity, she stages her own death to finally see who actually loves her versus who simply benefits from her.

**Why Nigerians are watching:** Funke Akindele's understanding of what Nigerian audiences respond to is unmatched. This film delivers exactly what her fanbase expects: recognisable characters, sharp humour, emotional depth, and a story that holds a mirror up to the dynamics many Nigerian families live inside. The casting of Scarlet Gomez in the lead role has also driven significant conversation.

**Cast:** Scarlet Gomez, Mercy Aigbe, Uzor Arukwe, Bimbo Akintola.

**Available now on Netflix Nigeria.**

---

### 5. The Covenant (Nollywood Crime Thriller Series)

Among the Nigerian originals trending on Netflix in early 2026, The Covenant stands out as the one drawing the most sustained conversation. Directed by the late Dimeji Ajibola, whose passing has made this series a bittersweet but essential watch, the show is described by critics and viewers alike as one of the most gripping Nollywood crime dramas ever committed to screen.

**What it is about:** A wealthy family's world is dismantled by a kidnapping that pulls them into a dark, layered web of militant gangs and occult secrets. Nothing about the situation is straightforward, and trust becomes the rarest commodity in every direction.

**Why Nigerians are watching:** The combination of family drama, organised crime, and occult mythology hits a very specific nerve in Nigerian storytelling culture. The series is tense, well-acted, and directed with a precision that reflects Ajibola's considerable talent. Watching it knowing it is among his final works adds an emotional texture that is difficult to separate from the experience.

**Cast:** Gideon Okeke, Sola Sobowale, Zubby Michael, Ivie Okujaye.

**Available now on Netflix Nigeria.**

---

### 6. Beef Season 2 (Dark Comedy Drama)

The original Beef series, which starred Ali Wong and Steven Yeun and swept awards season after its 2023 debut, returns with a new cast and a new conflict. Season 2 had a slow start in its debut week, but a 71% jump in viewing hours the following week confirmed that the audience found it on their own terms.

**What it is about:** A new road rage incident between two strangers in a different city spirals into an obsessive conflict that neither party can walk away from, drawing in everyone around them.

**Why Nigerians are watching:** The original series became a cultural phenomenon partly because of its willingness to portray the mundane triggers behind escalating conflict with both humour and genuine psychological depth. Nigerian audiences who found resonance in the first season have followed with curiosity into the second.

**Available now on Netflix.**

---

### 7. Son of the Soil (Nollywood Action Film)

One of the standout Nollywood films on Netflix Nigeria this April, Son of the Soil follows Zion Ladejo (Razaaq Adoti), a dishonourably discharged Nigerian Special Operations soldier who returns to Lagos from the United States after his sister's tragic death.

**What it is about:** Consumed by grief and haunted by his past, Zion launches a violent one-man campaign to find and dismantle the criminal network responsible for his sister's death. What follows is a Lagos-set action film that delivers on its promise: bone-crunching fights, chaotic Lagos market chase scenes, and an emotional undercurrent that keeps the action from feeling hollow.

**Why Nigerians are watching:** Nollywood action films that take themselves seriously and deliver technically competent fight choreography and location shooting are still rare enough to feel like events when they arrive. Son of the Soil is that kind of film. The Lagos setting, familiar and yet filmed with genuine cinematic ambition, makes it land differently for Nigerian audiences than an equivalent Hollywood production would.

**Cast:** Razaaq Adoti, and a strong supporting ensemble.

**Available now on Netflix Nigeria.**

---

### 8. Behind Her Eyes (Psychological Thriller, Returning to Nigerian Top 10)

This one is a throwback, and its return to the Nigerian Top 10 in 2026 has been driven almost entirely by a viral TikTok resurgence. Behind Her Eyes originally premiered on Netflix in 2021 and became famous for a finale twist that genuinely changed the internet for several weeks.

**What it is about:** Louise (Simona Brown), a single mother, begins an affair with her psychiatrist boss while simultaneously and secretly befriending his wife, Adele (Eve Hewson). What appears to be a conventional love triangle unravels into something considerably stranger, involving lucid dreaming, psychological control, and a final reveal that is genuinely difficult to see coming.

**Why Nigerians are watching in 2026:** The series has been resurfacing on TikTok through reaction videos, "don't tell me how it ends" posts, and first-watch commentary. New viewers who discover it through these clips are watching the full series and then immediately returning to social media to process the finale. This cycle has driven consistent chart presence weeks after the initial viral moment.

**Cast:** Simona Brown, Eve Hewson, Tom Bateman.

**Available now on Netflix.**

---

## A Note on What Nigerian Viewers Are Telling Netflix

The composition of the Nigerian Top 10 at any given moment tells a consistent story about what Nigerian viewers actually want from a streaming platform. It is not exclusively Nollywood, and it is not exclusively international. It is a deliberate mix: one or two globally dominant titles that Nigeria discovers alongside the rest of the world, one or two Nollywood originals or acquisitions that reflect specifically Nigerian storytelling, and one or two titles that have found their Nigerian audience through social media virality rather than editorial placement.

Nigerian viewers are also notably loyal to certain genres. Crime thrillers with Nigerian settings (The Covenant, Son of the Soil), psychological dramas with strong female protagonists (Behind Her Eyes, Unchosen, Behind the Scenes), and Nollywood comedies built around family and social dynamics (Behind the Scenes) consistently outperform more niche international offerings in the Nigerian charts.

The viral pipeline from TikTok to Netflix remains one of the most reliable discovery mechanisms on the platform for Nigerian audiences. A single well-timed TikTok clip of a shocking scene, a twist reveal, or a relatable character moment can push a title into the Top 10 weeks or months after its original release.

---

## Quick Watchlist Summary

| Title | Genre | Why to Watch |
|---|---|---|
| Unchosen | Psychological thriller | Global number one, gripping cult drama |
| Apex | Action thriller | Charlize Theron at her best, relentless pace |
| Running Point S2 | Sports comedy | Binge-worthy, sharp writing |
| Behind the Scenes | Nollywood comedy-drama | Highest-grossing Nollywood film ever |
| The Covenant | Nollywood crime thriller | Dimeji Ajibola's final masterpiece |
| Beef Season 2 | Dark comedy drama | Building momentum, original was unmissable |
| Son of the Soil | Nollywood action | Best Nigerian action film on the platform |
| Behind Her Eyes | Psychological thriller | The twist will haunt you |

---

## Conclusion

Netflix Nigeria in May 2026 is one of the most interesting it has been in years. The Nigerian Top 10 is genuinely representative of how Nigerian viewers actually watch: globally curious, culturally loyal, and heavily influenced by what is happening on social media at any given moment.

Whether you start with the globally viral Unchosen, the record-breaking Behind the Scenes, or the return of Behind Her Eyes through TikTok's long memory, you have a weekend's worth of exceptional content right there.

Stop scrolling. Pick one. You already know you are not going to sleep on time anyway.

*Chart positions and view counts sourced from Netflix Tudum, FlixPatrol, Variety, and What's on Netflix. All data correct as of 1 May 2026. Availability may vary by region.*
